candidates.title: Best neighborhoods in North San Antonio, honestly compared
candidates.query: best neighborhoods in north san antonio
candidates.hook: Most people relocating here get pointed to the same three areas up north, and two of them come with a commute or a school-boundary surprise nobody mentions until you're under contract. Here's how the north side actually breaks down.
candidates.outline:
Where the north side actually starts: Loop 410 to 1604, and why Castle Hills, Shavano Park and Stone Oak feel like three different cities
Inside 1604 for a Medical Center job: Oak Hills, Churchill Estates and Deerfield. older homes, mature trees, and the shortest drive to Floyd Curl and Wurzbach
Past 1604 on 281: Stone Oak, Encino Park and Timberwood Park. newer house, more square footage, and a US-281 commute you should drive before you sign
Northeast for Randolph AFB, Fort Sam Houston and BAMC: Live Oak, Selma, Universal City, Schertz and Cibolo, and what Schertz-Cibolo-Universal City ISD vs Judson ISD actually changes
The school-boundary surprise: Northside ISD and North East ISD split Stone Oak addresses, and Comal ISD reaches down into Timberwood Park and Cibolo Canyons. verify by address, not by subdivision name
VA buyers specifically: how the disabled veteran homestead exemption interacts with the MUD and PID assessments north of 1604, and which of these areas veterans tend to stay in versus resell out of
candidates.why: A family relocating for a job in the medical center or on the north side has a weekend house-hunting trip booked and needs to know which zip codes to spend it in.
candidates.footage: drive-through footage of older tree-lined streets versus newer subdivisions, 1604 traffic at rush hour, a school pickup line, aerial of the northern edge of development meeting open land

candidates.title: The truth about property taxes in Austin before you move here
candidates.hook: Texas has no state income tax, and people moving to Austin assume that means they come out ahead. Then they see the tax line on an Austin property and realize the money didn't disappear, it just moved to a different bill.
outline: Why your tax bill is stacked from several separate entities, not one
Homestead exemption: what it does, what it doesn't, and when to file
Why the tax on the house you buy may not match the tax the seller paid
MUD and PID districts in the outer suburbs and why two similar homes differ
How protests and appraisal caps actually work for a new owner
What to check before you make an offer
candidates.why: Someone relocating from a state with income tax is running their numbers this week and has just discovered the tax line item is larger than they budgeted for.
candidates.footage: close-ups of a tax statement with numbers blurred, county appraisal district office exterior, suburban streets in outer Austin, a laptop showing a public tax lookup page

candidates.title: Moving to Austin: which suburb fits how you actually work
candidates.query: moving to austin which suburb should i live in
candidates.hook: The suburb people pick before they move is almost never the one they'd pick after six months of driving it. The deciding factor isn't the house, it's which direction you have to travel on a Tuesday morning.
outline: North, south, east, west: what each direction of Austin is known for
If you go into an office: matching your suburb to where the employers are
If you're fully remote: what you gain by moving further out
Older established suburbs versus the new-growth edges
What changes when you cross a county or school district line
How to test-drive a suburb in one weekend visit
candidates.why: A remote or hybrid worker with a relocation date set is choosing between suburbs they've only seen on a map and doesn't yet know which drives will wear them down.
candidates.footage: highway footage in each direction at rush hour, contrast between an older suburban main street and a newly built subdivision, downtown office towers, a home office setup
